thread:
maria: quick sync 1 Acme verbally committed to a 3-month POC. We need a crisp capacity plan (reserved GPUs + autoscale policy), a presales pricing delta (4 vs 6 vs 8 reserved), and answers for the security questionnaire by EOD. Who can help with traffic shape and cost impact?

ben: tagging @carla @dmitri. can you share traffic profile details? avg/peak, seq length, model family?

carla: workload = public chat + embedding lookups. estimated steady QPS ~250, steady concurrency ~40 rps, short bursts up to ~2k QPS lasting ~10-20s, median tokens/request ~140, sessions ~3-5 turns. 95th pctl latency target = 300ms. planned model: 13B open-llama style, q4 quantized.

dmitri: sounds bursty. rough capacity calc: for steady 250 qps -> tokens/sec = 35k. With our measured 13B-q4 throughput ~18k toks/sec per GPU (depends on batching), baseline GPUs = ceil(35k/18k) = 2, add 20% headroom -> 3. For burst (2k qps -> 280k toks/sec) naive need ~16 GPUs. To avoid long cold starts, we recommend reserving 4 GPUs and autoscaling to higher counts with fast preheat.

carla: sales wants concrete numbers for reserved 4 vs 6 vs 8. can you produce a quick cost delta and risk summary?

dmitri: quick notes:
- reserved 4: lowest cost, reasonable for steady traffic; risk: queuing & >95p violations under full cache miss bursts unless autoscale is instant.
- reserved 6: balanced; covers modest bursts with less autoscale reliance.
- reserved 8: safer for frequent spikes; higher committed cost but reduces throttle risk.
Fallbacks: autoscale to burst pool (mix of reserved+spot), degraded path -> 7B quantized variant (~2x throughput), soft-throttle with Retry-After header.

ben: can KV/prefix caching and microbatching reduce the burst GPU requirement? yes. with high cache-hit ratio we often see ~2-3x effective throughput improvement. so 16 -> ~6 GPUs in optimistic caching scenario. also can limit max response tokens during bursts.

carla: good. action items for presales doc: capacity table (4/6/8), autoscale policy sample, KV warmup checklist, fallback wording for legal. ben, drop an autoscale snippet.

ben: sample policy (infra config snippet):
````
autoscale_policy:\n  min_reserved: 4\n  max_scale: 16\n  scale_metric: tokens_per_sec\n  scale_up_threshold: 0.75\n  scale_down_cooldown: 2m\n  preheat_on_scale: true\n  fallback_model: "13B-q4lite-fallback"\n  throttle: {soft_429: true, retry_after_secs: 5}\n````

maria: perfect. security Q asks about KMS, VPC, and audit logs. dmitri, can you confirm what Dedicated/Private provide?

dmitri: yes. summary for questionnaire: customer-managed KMS supported, VPC peering or PrivateLink for Dedicated, audit logs exportable to S3/CloudWatch, role-based access controls, and TLS in transit. I'll attach a one-pager and confirm SLA language.

carla: i'll compile POC runbook: recommended reserve (we'll propose 4 reserved, autoscale to 12 with burst credits, fallback to smaller model), cost delta table, autoscale snippet, KV warmup steps, security one-pager, and a short legal-friendly fallback paragraph.

maria: timeline 1 need a draft for presales by 1700 PT so finance can price. can you all confirm delivery times?

ben: will paste perf numbers and expected token/sec per GPU by 1500.

dmitri: will upload security one-pager and preheat commands + AZ spread recommendations by 1600.

carla: will assemble the doc and cost table and send by 1630, including fallback phrasing for contracts.

deploy-bot: preheat job queued: job_id=preheat-1712345678-1, target_gpus=4, kv_warmup=true

maria: thanks team 1 i'll update the customer and sync with finance after we have numbers. :thumbsup:
